1. The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.12,50,000/- for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 08.12.2016.

It is pertinent to note that the preset matter is disposed on dated 10.07.2018 and thereafter the petitioner and respondent No.2 being aggrieved by impugned Judgment and award dated 10.07.2018 as preferred MFA No.8022/2018 and 2267/2019 respectively before Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and as per the order dated 02.12.2024 in that matters the Hon'ble High M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 Court of Karnataka set-aside the impugned Judgment and Award dated 10.07.2018 and remanded the matter to this court.
2.

It is the case of the petitioner that, on 08.12.2016 at about 1-15 p.m., within the jurisdiction of Doddabelavangala Police Station, near land property of Jayaram, Ajjanakatte NH 207 Road,
Doddaballapura - Dabaspete road when the Petitioner was riding the unoffending Motor Cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-03-ED- 2233, at that time the accused drove the offending Auto Rickshaw bearing Reg. No.KA-43-6206 from Doddabelavangala towards Doddaballapura in a rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and without giving any indications suddenly turned the vehicle towards right side and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result he sustained grievous bleeding injuries.

Thereafter Petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital,
Doddaballapura and for higher treatment he was shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bangalore wherein he was treated as inpatient and undergone surgery therein and he has spent Rs.2,80,000/- towards medical expenditure and other incidental charges.
In this regard the informant/Idayathpasha has lodged complaint before the Doddabelavangala police station.

Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.205/2016 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279 and 338 of IPC and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the investigating Officer.
3. Further it is contended that, prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner was hale, healthy and he was aged about 34 years and he was working as driver and earning sum of Rs.17,000/- p.m.

Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident he lost his income and future prospective life,
happiness, and earning capacity and become disabled and dependent.
The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending Auto bearing registration No.KA-43-6206.

On going through the prosecution papers,
FIR, mahazar, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.

The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
It seems that Pw.1 has clearly made those versions, which could not be shattered in cross examination.

Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot without giving any indications suddenly turned the vehicle towards right side and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The evidence of Pw.1, Ex.P-1/FIR, Ex.P-2/Complaint, Ex.P4/spot Mahazar, Ex.P-5/MVA report, Ex.P- 3/Wound Certificate and Ex.P.6/Charge Sheet clearly establishes that the alleged accident occurred at the spot.

It is not in dispute as to the aspect that,
the Petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the alleged M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 incident.
Because, for the above reasons collectively it is clear that, the accident happened due to rash and negligent act of the accused.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P3/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 and 338 of IPC.

Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

24. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused.

In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was working as driver and earning M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 Rs.17,000/- p.m., he has not produced single piece of document to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.

As per the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, for the accident taken place in the year 2016, the notional income of the Petitioner is taken at Rs.8,750/-.

In the chief examination of PW-3/Dr.Chethan.A., Consultant Orthopedic Surgeon deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has sustained open fracture distal femur left,

sentences.text: With regard to the quantum, the age of the petitioner is considered as 34 years and the income is considered at Rs.8,750/- p.m.
As per Sarala Varma's Case the multiplier 16 is applicable and functional disability is considered at 20%.

On considering the avocation and age of the petitioner,
the total loss of future income is calculated as (Rs.8,750/- X 12 X 16 X 20/100) = Rs.3,36,000/-.
Hence, an amount of Rs.3,36,000/- is awarded to the petitioner under the head loss of future income for the disability suffered by him in the accident.

28. In the alleged accident the petitioner has sustained sustained open fracture distal femur left,
fracture of interior pole of patella left and comminuted fracture both bones of left forearm and he undergone ORIF with LCP left femur on 08.12.2016, ORIF - TBW left patella on 08.12.2016 and ORIF both bones of left forearm on M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 08.12.2016, which shows that definitely the petitioner has suffered pain due to the injuries sustained in the accident, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards pain and suffering, mental agony.

29. Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient at Hosmat Hospital for a period from 08.12.2016 to 12.12.2016, i.e., for a period of 5 days.
Therefore this court deems it appropriate to award Rs.15,000/- (Rs.3,000/- per day X 5 days) under head of special diet and conveyance.
30. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has suffered uncomfortable in his day to day life, hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities.
31. Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the Petitioner would require atleast six months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore the Petitioner would be entitled to Rs.52,500/- (Rs.8,750/- x 6 months) under the head loss of income during laid up period.
32. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical expenses as per Ex.P.8 for an amount of M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 Rs.2,44,069/-.

On going through the Ex.P.8 medical bill in Sl.

Hence Sl. No.7, 21,
33, 34 35 and 36 cannot be considered to grant compensation under the head of medical expenses.

The Counsel for respondent No.2/insurance company contended that the offending vehicle is not covered with the valid insurance policy as on the date of the alleged accident, as such they are not liable to pay the compensation amount.

The respondent No.1 contended that the offending vehicle was duly insured with Respondent No.2/Insurance company as on the date of the alleged accident and any liability, i.e., fastened on him would have to be indemnify by the Respondent No.2.

The petitioner contended that the offending vehicle is covered with the valid insurance policy as on the date of the alleged accident and filed memo producing the valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle and on going through the said insurance policy of the offending vehicle it is seen that the offending vehicle was duly M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 insured with the respondent No.2 insurance company as on the date of the alleged accident.
Hence the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the award amount.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2/Insurance Company and it is directed to deposit the compensation amount.
Thus I conclude that, the Insurance company/Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount along with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of filing of the claim petition.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 in the affirmative.
37. Issue No.3:

In the result I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the Petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Partly allowed with cost.

The Petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.9,39,529/-
(Rupees Nine Lakhs Thirty Nine Thousand Five Hundred and Twenty Nine only)
with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 Amount awarded under the future medical expenses does not carry future interest.
Further, Respondent No.2 being insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to deposit the compensation amount together with 6% interest within 60 days from the date of this order.
After deposit, entire compensation amount with interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner under E-payment with proper verification and identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Petitioner sustained grievous injuries due to alleged accident caused by the offending vehicle in question.
6 Petitioner and no fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, however, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent.
On going through the prosecution papers,
FIR, mahazar, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet and the evidence of PW-1 is specific to the effect that, the driver of the offending vehicle/accused is the reason for the said incident and at his instance, the incident took place.
The alleged accident was occurred due to rash and M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
The evidence of Pw.1 was corroborated to the case of the prosecution and he has supported the manner of occurrence in his evidence in the court and the manner of occurrence is the same as alleged in the Ex.P2/complaint.
Therefore, considering the above discussed aspects collectively, it is the considered opinion of the Court that, the incident having been taken place in the manner asserted by the prosecution and the same being proved to have been taken place in the manner alleged by the prosecution, the accused drew the offending vehicle in a high speed, rash or negligent manner so as to endanger human life and at the spot without giving any indications suddenly turned the vehicle towards right side and dashed against the unoffending vehicle, as a result Petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
It is evident that injuries noted in the Ex.P3/Wound Certificate would be caused by a road accident.
At the same time, it has come out in evidence that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle and fault of the accused.
Matters being so, the acts of the accused person clearly constitute the offences punishable under sections 279 and 338 of IPC.
Thus because of such negligent act of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle, it resulted in the injuries of the innocent man/Petitioner aforesaid, as he/accused drove the said offending vehicle very rashly or negligently on the spot.
Therefore, the alleged accident occurred due to the fault of the accused/driver of the offending vehicle.
In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was working as driver and earning M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 Rs.17,000/- p.m., he has not produced single piece of document to prove his actual income.
In the absence of proof of income the notional income has to be assessed.
But due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident the petitioner has not in position to do M.V.C.No.8282/2016 SCCH - 7 work as past.
